note: Best gyros in town, or a close second. We're not arguing with the pita.
Skip the Coke. Still the one. We'll be back.
Julia's. Cool, clean, cucumber down the glass.
Whole fish off the grill, lemon, tomato, herbs. Tonight's seafood.
Barley rusks, tomato, onion, cucumber, and a pile of cheese. The table before the fish.
Still hot from the oil, drenched in honey, walnuts, and cinnamon. Best loukoumades in town. We ate them walking.
A whole wall of pomegranates, then they squeeze it in front of you. Bright, tart, no sugar needed. Best juice we've had in Greece.
Skewers and a charred sausage, thick fries, tzatziki, and grilled bread. The guy at the grill gave us two thumbs up. Best souvlaki in Chania. Five stars.
From coffee to beer, same table, same view. We haven't moved. Gotta love Crete.
Cured meats, cheese, figs, walnuts, olives — and a placemat that asked what a whole bottle could do for the heart.
Grilled skewers, thick-cut fries, spicy dip, and cold Alfa with the old harbour behind us. Lunch done right.
Tomatoes, onion, olives, and a slab of feta with oregano — proper village salad by the water.
Two frothy iced coffees and cold mountain water with the Venetian harbour behind us. First proper morning in Crete.

place: Pork to Beef Wild, Chania area
note: First meal in Greece — juicy, herbed fries, and exactly what we needed after landing. Delicious.

place: Guy Fieri’s Kitchen + Bar Express, Burbank Airport
note: Cold cans, gate-side, official DDIC kickoff before the flight to Crete.
